Traced the precedence chain myself rather than trusting the finding. config.Load (internal/platform/config/loader.go:13-32) is Default() -> FromEnv() -> FromFlags() -> Validate(). Default() sets Server.ListenAddr = "127.0.0.1:8080" (defaults.go:14) and Mode.WebPort = 8081 (defaults.go:9); ModeConfig.WebMode has no default entry, so it is the zero value false. FromEnv touches ListenAddr only through envString("HTTP_LISTEN_ADDR", ...) at loader.go:106, and envString assigns only when the value is non-empty (loader.go:34-38) — .env.example:55 ships HTTP_LISTEN_ADDR="". FromFlags binds -web to Mode.WebMode (loader.go:233) and -port to Mode.WebPort (loader.go:234), then re-derives ListenAddr to 0.0.0.0:<WebPort> *only inside* `if cfg.Mode.WebMode` (loader.go:252-258). `git grep -nE 'ListenAddr' 06d9f8ce -- internal cmd` shows the complete set of writers: defaults.go:14, loader.go:106/254/256 — nothing else — and Validate() is not among them. cmd/slabledger/server.go:217-220 falls back to Mode.WebPort only when addr == "", which the non-empty default makes unreachable. Therefore bare `./slabledger` binds 127.0.0.1:8080, and `slabledger server --port 9090` parses -port into Mode.WebPort which nothing then reads. Doc leg confirmed independently: README.md:21-22 (`./slabledger` / `# Open http://localhost:8081`), CLAUDE.md:10, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:256, and cmd/slabledger/main.go showHelp() which advertises both `slabledger` -> 'default port 8081' and `slabledger server --port 9090`. Every working invocation passes --web (Makefile:48, Makefile:51, Dockerfile:98), which is exactly why the drift is invisible. The consequence also holds: web/vite.config.js:56/61 proxy to localhost:8081 and .devcontainer/docker-compose.yml:61 publishes 8081:8081, so the documented invocation additionally binds a loopback address that the published port cannot reach. I did not treat CLAUDE.md as an authority; it is one of the four wrong documents.

Attacked this hardest because confirming it means the gated Phase 1 config map is wrong. `jq '.records[] | select(.identity|test("WebMode"))' maps/config-map.json` shows the record kind is literally `config_field_dead` with external_refs 0 and ref_sites [] — so the map's classification is as the finding describes. My own `git grep -nE '\bWebMode\b' 06d9f8ce` returns exactly seven live-source hits: types.go:7 (declaration), loader.go:233, loader.go:252, config.go:24, config.go:25, config_test.go:83, config_test.go:171 — the map's count of zero *external* refs is arithmetically right. The conclusion is what fails. loader.go:233 `fs.BoolVar(&cfg.Mode.WebMode, "web", ...)` is preamble mechanism 7: the setter is a command-line token, which no Go grep can see. Two live setters exist outside Go, both verified by me: Dockerfile:98 `CMD ["--web", "--port", "8081"]` — the command every deployed container runs — and Makefile:48/51. cmd/slabledger/main.go additionally special-cases `case "--web": mode = "server"` in its argv dispatch. And the field gates real behavior: loader.go:252-258 is the sole path by which Mode.WebPort ever reaches Server.ListenAddr (cross-checked against the complete ListenAddr writer set in my DCT-002 basis). Deleting WebMode would move every deployed container from 0.0.0.0:8081 to 127.0.0.1:8080. LIVE, not dead; the map's single dead-field entry is a false positive.

The finding's first evidence entry claims 'Every one of the six describe blocks in the spec is gated on RUN_VISUAL_REGRESSION.' It is not. I counted by reading the source, not by substring: `git show 06d9f8ce:web/tests/e2e/visual-regression.spec.ts | grep -nE 'describe\(|test\(|test.skip|toHaveScreenshot'` gives six describes at lines 46, 84, 122, 133, 169, 195 and only five test.skip guards at 50, 126, 137, 173, 199. Reading lines 84-119 in full: `test.describe('Visual Regression - Components @visual')` has a beforeEach and two tests and NO skip guard at all. Those two tests are 'Header navigation' (toHaveScreenshot('header-navigation.png'), :98) and 'Search form' (toHaveScreenshot('search-form.png'), :114) — which are precisely the two names carried by the ten committed baselines under web/tests/e2e/visual-regression.spec.ts-snapshots/, five per name, one per Playwright project. Those baselines are live: browser-matrix.yml:82/84/174 runs the unfiltered suite per browser and per device, which is why five project-specific PNGs exist for each. So the third evidence claim ('They can never be compared against anything') and the fourth ('none of which has ever run in CI at this revision') are both false. What does survive, verified independently: `git grep -n 'RUN_VISUAL_REGRESSION' 06d9f8ce` returns five hits, all guards in that one spec, and nothing sets the variable — no workflow, no Makefile target, no package.json script, no .env.example entry. So 4 of 6 describe blocks and 6 of 8 toHaveScreenshot assertions are gated on a variable with no setter anywhere in the tree. That is a real but much smaller defect than filed.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Three of its four evidence claims are wrong about scope. The 'Visual Regression - Components' describe block (visual-regression.spec.ts:84) carries no gate, so 2 of the 8 screenshot assertions DO execute in CI, and the ten committed baseline PNGs are live comparison targets, not orphans. The correct statement is: 6 of 8 screenshot assertions (4 of 6 describe blocks) are permanently skipped because RUN_VISUAL_REGRESSION is set nowhere. I am marking this not ticketable because a fixer acting on the filed text — in particular its acceptance criterion 'If removed: git grep -n RUN_VISUAL_REGRESSION returns empty' — could delete the ten baselines that the browser matrix is actually asserting against on every run. Re-scope before ticketing.

basis: Deliberately avoided the substring trap the preamble warns about: I read both files rather than counting greps. `git show 06d9f8ce:internal/integration/dh_search_diag_test.go | grep -nE '^func Test|t.(Error|Fatal|Fail|Skip)|require.|assert.'` returns three Test functions (:17, :83, :132) and zero assertion hits of any kind; the same on dh_match_search_test.go returns five Test functions (:66, :111, :158, :224, :296) with t.Fatalf hits only at :252 and :272, both inside TestDHMatchSearch_SearchThenMatch (:224) — so the other four are assertion-free. That is the finding's seven, by name, established by my own route. Reading the body at dh_search_diag_test.go:52-70 confirms the swallow: `if err != nil { t.Logf("ERROR: %v", err); return }` — an API failure is logged and returned from. The table at :19-49 has 15 entries, each running a live c.SearchCards inside t.Run. The CI leg holds too: .github/workflows/test.yml has `schedule: cron '0 6 * * *'`, the integration job is gated `if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || workflow_dispatch`, a preceding step hard-fails when any of the five credentials is missing, and the run step is `go test -race -v -timeout 20m -tags integration ./internal/integration/...` — the whole package, with real DH_ENTERPRISE_API_KEY. internal/integration/dh_enterprise_test.go:18-29 shows newDHEnterpriseClient t.Skips only when the key is absent, which CI guarantees it is not. So these seven make live third-party calls daily and are structurally incapable of going red. Baseline counts also reconcile: 243 tracked *_test.go files and 1376 top-level Test functions, both matching the finding exactly.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: One qualifier, not a defect in the finding's core: the word 'paid' in 'consume paid DH Enterprise calls' is not establishable by static analysis — nothing in the repository states DH Enterprise metering or pricing, and I did not run the suite. What IS statically established is that the calls are live, third-party, daily, and at least 15 in one function alone. The finding stands on that leg; a ticket should say 'live API calls on a daily schedule' rather than assert a quota cost.

basis: `git grep -nE '\b(it|test|describe).(skip|todo)\b|\bxit\(' 06d9f8ce -- web/src web/tests` returns exactly seven hits: ErrorBoundary.test.jsx:327 and :337, five RUN_VISUAL_REGRESSION guards in visual-regression.spec.ts, and screenshot-all-pages.spec.ts:167 gated on SCREENSHOT_BACKEND. So the two ErrorBoundary skips are the only unconditional ones, as claimed. Reading web/tests/components/ErrorBoundary.test.jsx:324-346 directly confirms both are bare `it.skip(...)` with no condition argument, under a `describe('development mode')` whose comment gives the reason: 'import.meta.env.DEV is a build-time constant in Vite / It cannot be changed at test runtime'. The dev-vs-prod error-detail branch is consequently unexercised. Correctly filed as `strong` rather than `mechanical` — the finding's own exclusion states the vi.stubEnv claim was not checked against the installed Vitest, and I did not check it either (that would require reading package.json/vitest config and, to be certain, running the suite, which is out of scope here).
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing material, but a note for the fixer that the finding does not mention: the two skipped tests have identical bodies (render <ErrorBoundary><BrokenComponent/></ErrorBoundary>) with opposite expectations, so under any single build mode at most one of them can pass as written. Re-enabling them requires rewriting, not just un-skipping — which makes the filed acceptance criterion 'inverting the ErrorBoundary's dev-mode condition makes at least one of the two tests fail' weaker than it reads. Ticketable, but the fixer must rewrite both bodies.

basis: The file-content half is accurate — `git show 06d9f8ce:docs/polish-report.md` is exactly two lines ('# Polish-All Report' / 'Base commit: ec4d261b... | Started: 2026-04-20') and `git ls-tree -r -l` gives 96 bytes. The orphan half fails, and it is an absence claim, so it needed a command with empty output. The finding records `git grep -n 'polish-report' 06d9f8ce -- ':!docs/audit'` as '(second command: empty — no inbound reference anywhere outside this audit's own artifacts)'. I ran that exact command and it exits 0 with five hits, all in a tracked file: .claude/skills/polish-all/SKILL.md:60, :97, :249, :277, :295. I re-ran it unfiltered (`git grep -n 'polish-report' 06d9f8ce`) and got the same five. The references are not incidental — SKILL.md:97 says 'If docs/polish-report.md doesn't exist (or --fresh), create it with:', :249 and :277 append to it, and :60 reads and prints it under --report. The file is therefore the live checkpoint artifact of a tracked skill that recreates it on demand, not an orphan. The finding's own acceptance criterion 'No document links to it — git grep -n polish-report returns empty outside .gitignore' cannot be satisfied without also editing that skill, which the finding neither mentions nor scopes.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The load-bearing claim, 'nothing links to it', is false, and the evidence entry asserting an empty grep does not reproduce — the command returns five hits in .claude/skills/polish-all/SKILL.md, which both creates and reads the file. Refuted per the brief's rule that an absence claim requires a command whose output is actually empty. Whatever residue is left (a 96-byte stub committed from an April 2026 tool run) is cosmetic and its removal is coupled to a skill definition the finding does not account for.
